title: Настя разоблачает Шефа  (Nastya Confronts the Chef)

segments.t: Outraged on Elena Pavlovna's behalf, Nastya confronts Chef Barinov outside the hotel room. When she hears a man's voice inside, Barinov claims they are secretly playing poker, but Nastya doesn't buy it and reaches for her phone.
А, так вы играете в покер.
Только не говори об этом Елене.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'How can you cheat on Elena?' Nastya wonders briskly in their exchange, pairing "kak" ("how") with "mozhete" ("can, may") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Sorry, Chef, I gave you away.' Kostya presents a sharp tone in this beat, leaning on "izvinite" ("sorry, excuse me") before closing the thought with "sdal" ("gave up, ratted out").
'I am in there with Elena Pavlovna.' Barinov sustains a firm line during the exchange, weaving "tam" ("there") together with "yelenoy" ("pavlovna") just the way native speakers do.
'Kostya, let us go, we will not disturb them.' Nastya brings a steady approach during the exchange, leaning on "poydyom" ("let's go") before closing the thought with "budem" ("will").
'Is there another man in there with you?' Nastya probes wryly as the talk turns, placing "tam" ("there") straight beside "yeshchyo" ("more, still") with no word for "to be" needed.
'Chef, are you going to win it back today?' Kostya tests plainly across the room, weaving "otygryvatsya" ("to win back") together with "segodnya" ("today") just the way native speakers do.
А, так вы играете в покер.
'Ah, so you are playing poker.' Kostya establishes a wry angle on the spot, combining "igrayete" ("play") and "poker" ("poker") so the key meaning lands right away.
Только не говори об этом Елене.
'Just do not tell Elena about this.' Barinov maintains an emphatic course toward Nastya, joining "tolko" ("only") to "govori" ("say, talk") so every word pulls its weight.
'I promised that I would quit soon.' Barinov projects a firm manner right away, weaving "obeshchal" ("promised") together with "skoro" ("soon") just the way native speakers do.
'Then what woman ordered champagne?' Nastya quizzes boldly as the beat lands, weaving "zhenshchina" ("woman") together with "shampanskoye" ("champagne") just the way native speakers do.
'We are leaving here, Kostik.' Nastya strikes a natural tone in front of Barinov, weaving "ukhodim" ("are leaving") together with "otsyuda" ("from here") just the way native speakers do.
'I am calling Elena Pavlovna right now.' Nastya displays a warm tack across the room, pairing "seychas" ("now") with "zvonyu" ("call") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
А, так вы играете в покер.
Только не говори об этом Елене.
To stop Nastya from calling Elena or the police, the chefs end up tying Kostya and Nastya up in the hotel room too. See you next time!
